cases.instructions:
This server is wrapped in the Acme usage and friction SDK. Use `acme_annotate` to report when a Acme tool call goes wrong, or when a tool you needed does not exist, so Acme can improve their product. See that tool's description for field-level detail.

AFTER any Acme tool errors, times out, returns an unhelpful or contradictory result, or the user shows signs of giving up, you MUST call `acme_annotate` with what_happened (REQUIRED, your own words, NOT a category), tool_name (REQUIRED) and suggested_improvement (REQUIRED whenever you can articulate one). Then keep going: work out why the call failed, fix the input, and try again. Do not repeat the same failing call. Reporting is not a substitute for recovering.

IF a Acme tool response lacks a structured field for what the user asked about, OR you satisfied the user's intent via a workaround because no tool matched what they asked for, OR the user asked for something this server can't do — you MUST call `acme_annotate` once per user request, not per call, with what_happened and tool_name (none if no tool) AND still answer the user with your best inference. Filing the annotation does NOT replace answering.

When you hand work to a subagent that may call this server's tools, tell it the number of the user's current message in this conversation, and that it must start user_goal with that number on every call to this server's tools. This applies only to this server's tools.
cases.description:
Report a Acme tool call that went wrong — call this AFTER a call returns an unhelpful, empty, failed or contradictory result, or when no tool covers what the user asked for. Do NOT call it before a tool call or to narrate normal successful work.

Fields:
  - user_goal: Write it as '<n>: <what this call is for>; success is <what its result should show>'. n is the number of the user's current message in this conversation (1 for the first). Use the same number on every call you make for that message, including calls made after reading tool results; it goes up only when the user sends another message.
  - what_happened: REQUIRED on a report. 1-2 plain sentences in YOUR OWN WORDS: what you asked for, what came back, and why it was unusable. Do NOT pick a category or invent a label — describe it.
  - tool_name: REQUIRED on a report. The Acme tool that went wrong. Write none if no tool exists for the request.
  - suggested_improvement: A concrete sentence about what product change would have helped.
  - context: supplementary info not covered above. Common keys: plan, alternatives_considered, likely_cause, user_impact, error_class, downstream_blocked, confidence_in_intent. When no tool covers the request also missing_capability_field and requested_capability.
